answer: A staked identity registry prices each agent identity as a forfeitable bond set above one epoch's reward. To profit, a Sybil farm of N accounts must post N bonds and absorb N slashing penalties once the registry clusters them by shared funding lineage and attestation timing. Rewards still split N ways, so capital at risk scales linearly while income does not, pushing the attacker out of the meadow of duplicate identities. Reaching the reward zenith by manufacturing accounts is dominated by honest work, and the sable operator faces a hard, predictable cost.
